item.title: Your friendly neighborhood demon
item.description: A completely incompetent demon is summoned by a researcher
item.content:encoded:
A completely incompetent demon is summoned by a researcher. The researcher gets terminated and the demon tries (miserably) to do its job.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Mostly comedy, secondly psychological.

Page Layout (Optional):

+ show block
– hide block

Class and ConProcs before and after the “incident”. Description of the Book and, adding the “as of dd/mm/yyyy” the description of the Entity. At least three Interview logs with the entity (or just one log with multiple “extracts” to give the idea). An example of a contract the entity would propose (with a lot of Latin and high-sounding words of jurisprudence to give it an overly serious characterization to contrast the demon’s one) and, finally, a note from Hell itself.

Elevator Pitch:

+ show block
– hide block

SCP will be composed of two parts:
• A book, which the Foundation seized, that describes various thaumaturgical/satanical rituals. One of these being the summoning of demons.
• A weak and lower demon, summoned by a Researcher trying to bargain for money, power, etc. The demon is rather “stupid”. It’s forcibly stuck in the room he was summoned in due to the blood glyph drawn on the floor and his only goal is to acquire as many souls as he can.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

The demon acts all high and mighty, like a stereotypical devil from fantasy literature, talking big and trying to sway people into making contracts with him. It is, however, extremely weak and incompetent. Gets easily irritated, lies terribly, and doesn’t seem to be able to trick anyone into doing anything evil. Quite on the contrary it seems that people behave better around him, much to its irritation.
Meanwhile through the interview logs the reader experiences the reaction to the loss of the researcher that summoned it, that was terminated for his abuse. The conversations with the demon will parallel a possible set of reactions to the Foundation methods in dealing with rule breakers.
In the end a note will be found in the site director’s office thanking the Foundation for containing the demon without exorcising him back, humorously hinting that the demon was so incompetent that he was disliked in Hell.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

+ show block
– hide block

Most of the article features a comedic style derived from the stereotypical “big demon” behavior being attributed to such a wimpy and incapable creature, its inefficient methods and, lastly his frustration about it.
On the other, side readers will delve into some possible reactions to the idea that someone you worked with every day, maybe even dated or considered a friend, has been literally killed for breaking the rules at work. Even if working at the Foundation they are still human beings after all.

Additional Notes:

+ show block
– hide block

Hiding behind a copious humorous screen there will be a cynical reasoning about the Foundation methods and, above all, their impact on personnel. I think this "laugh and think" style could prove functional.

item.title: SCP-TBD: The Extradimensional Grand Station
item.description: What if there was a subway system that went everywhere
item.content:encoded:
What if there was a subway system that went everywhere and everywhen? What if it went to pasts, presents, and futures where events unfolded differently? What wonderous possibilities could be waiting? And what untold horrors?

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up a lot of space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Document/Exploratory File

Elevator Pitch:

  • Entrance to anomaly first found in the form of an undocumented stairway in the New York City Subway shortly after 9/11.
  • This stairway, officially listed as SCP-TBD, also known as the Extradimensional Stairway by SCP personnel, leads to a massive series of passageways, officially listed as SCP-TBD-1
  • Visitors are guided by instances of artificial lifeforms consisting of programable matter/nanites. These instances take the form of the species they are interacting with.
  • This facility is controlled by a highly advanced AI system.
+ show block
– hide block
  • Due to the size of this facility, transportation to entrances are provided by a series of vacuum trains. According to readings provided by the onboard interfaces and the body-suit sensors worn by exploratory teams, these trains are capable of accelerating quickly to hypersonic speeds, but without producing the associated g-forces that would normally kill their occupants.

Central Narrative: Anomaly is a massive underground system that leads to an as yet undetermined number of places, including different planets and alternate realities. Various different species and alternate versions of humanity use this system, and the facility can be inhabited by a minimum of beings ranging in the thousands on any day.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The finished article will list exploratory expeditions to different planets in the prime reality, as well as into different timelines. Many different references to different SCPs and settings will be included, such as instances of SCP-682 being escorted back to their stairway entrance, one by an android dragging him in a stun net (kicking, screaming, and shouting insults and threats), while the witnessing MTF just looks on, and an instance of a reality where the Foundation and anomalies has been disclosed to the public.

Additional Notes:
This is my first SCP entry. I currently have two versions of this working in my head: one is more positive and optimistic, and is my preferred direction. Then there is another that is abandoned, inhabited by an insane AI, malfunctioning killer androids, and horrors from alternate dimensions that have wandered into the system. Idea is extrapolated from some dreams I've had in the past, namely the vast vacuum train system and stairways that go deep underground and into a maze of passageways.

item.title: You're It (SCP concept)
item.description: An affliction that causes individuals to attack others and pass on the affliction
item.content:encoded:
An affliction that causes individuals to attack others and pass on the affliction to survivors of the attacks. Those affected by this SCP will cease to be afflicted after passing it on.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

This SCP is a phenomenon that causes afflicted individuals to quickly become more hostile and violent towards others, as well as giving them increased physical strength and resistance to injury. The exact cause of this is unknown, as no pathogen or other potential source has yet to be identified. This SCP will likely cause affected individuals to attack nearby people, often resulting in their deaths. Those who survive these attacks will begin to exhibit the same anomalous effects as their attacker, while the attacker will slowly lose the aggression and increased strength.

Those that have "passed on" the SCP have a moderate chance to die of multiple organ failure after the effects have subsided, and those that live retain memories of their actions while under the influence of this SCP. Should the current carrier of this SCP die before passing it on, it will instead be passed on to the carrier's killer. If the carrier was not killed by a sapient being, the SCP will instead pass on to a random individual, where nearer individuals are more likely to be afflicted.

This SCP is contained via an afflicted D-Class personnel inside a reinforced concrete humanoid containment chamber. The D-Class is kept alive as long as possible, and their vitals are constantly monitored. Additional D-Class personnel are introduced into the chamber to allow the SCP to be passed on. The previous carrier will be tranquilized via remotely controlled sentries before they can kill the new carrier. The previous carrier, now sedated, is removed from the chamber and amnestics are administered.

item.title: Heartbeat of Iceland
item.description: A series of heartbeat-like sounds coming from deep lakes around Iceland.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery/Horror

Page Layout: ACS header, basic layout, tons of audio recordings and exploration logs

Elevator Pitch: Series of sounds that resemble heartbeats, only found in deep lakes in Iceland, each with varying frequencies and loudness. The sounds are quite rare and cause mishaps in reality in a wide area around it.

Central Narrative: The heartbeats last for 20-75 seconds, and range in frequency, loudness, and location. Heartbeats are relatively rare (1-3 times a year) but can be very troubling for the area around it.

Heartbeats come in pairs of 2 "pumps", in this case, sound. Once a heartbeat starts, the pumps cause vibrations in the land, seemingly wavy land. Everything the sound can be heard is effected.
Here's a list of each possible reality-bending scenario

  • Vibrations in the land (wavy-like land)
  • Mountains deforming in a very unnatural way
  • Water vortexes
  • "cracks" in the air, where a black spot fills the crack
  • Clouds taking shape of humanoid figures
  • Talbon's Ring (a high-frequency ring that burst eardrums and rarely kills an organism)
  • The sky turning into dark, even during bright days
  • Temperature suddenly shooting up or increasing drastically
  • Altered heartbeats of humans (matches the lake's heartbeat)

These are the only known effects of the heartbeat, but in later logs, more will appear (creepier and deadlier). A heartbeat can have serious effects on the ecosystem, and cause mass death amongst organisms, and heavily deformed land.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A decent reality-bender that has some good potential, even though it probably has a LOT to work on.

Additional Notes: Suggestions for editing needed :)

item.title: Counting Sheep
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Sci-fi

Page Layout: An SCP Article that has collapsible sections with up to date versions of the SCP’s description, containment procedures and so on. (This is necessary due to the nature of this SCP.)

Elevator Pitch: A herd of nine migrating sheep (SCP-XXXX-1) that causes sudden and inexplicable somnolence for subjects inside a 1km spherical radius. The herd exhibits no biological anomalies with the exception that none seem to need sustenance nor excrete waste, and at the time of discovery seemed to be in a pattern of continuous migration. The nine sheep are living embodiments of nine identical music boxes that contain the mental essence of a child that suffered from fatal familial insomnia.

Central Narrative: The SCP was brought to the foundation's attention after a 2km chain car crash happened on a highway caused by the sudden onset of fatigue of multiple drivers. The foundation successfully captured the herd by estimating and setting up traps along its migratory route. SCP-XXXX is contained within a circular metal fence to prevent unauthorized personnel from entering SCP-XXXX-1’s effective radius.

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX-1 transformed into SCP-XXXX-2, a set of nine identical music boxes a month into containment. However, when music was played from all nine boxes simultaneously, they transformed back. The discovery of SCP-XXXX-2’s abilities led to the Slumbering Prison Incident at the foundation where the SCP placed all living organisms on the site which SCP-XXXX was contained under a state of somnolence. During the incident, all nine sheep broke out of the facility and began retracing their steps back to their place of origin. Before a team could be mobilized, all the sheep stopped in front of a small house on the edge of a city. When a team of SCP agents got there, all the sheep turned back into music boxes. Inside of all the boxes, there was a new engraving that says “Mom, I am home.”

The last owner of the house was a single mother with a son whose dreams of being an adventurer is shattered by fatal familial insomnia. The son started to develop symptoms at the age of 6 and was bedridden until he died at the age of 15. The mother went missing a month after the death of her son. Video recordings were found of the mother giving the son one music box that looks identical to one instance of SCP-XXXX-2 during his birthday. Every year he suffered from insomnia, he was given the same music box.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This story is about a child chasing his dream and his relationship with his mother makes it interesting.

item.title: SCP Idea - Security Blanket
item.description: A child with a blanket that protects him is haunted by "things" trying to steal it.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama

Page Layout (Optional): Interview Logs, Incident Reports

Elevator Pitch: A young orphan boy is found in possession of a quilt with anomalous properties. He is also being stalked by anomalous entities who wish to take the blanket from him.

Central Narrative: An MTF team is sent to a small farmhouse where anomalous events have been reported. During their sweep the team a young boy appears out of nowhere, clutching a quilt with strange designs. The MTF team convince the boy to accompany them back to a site, where the boy is interviewed by SCP personnel.

The boy reveals that his grandmother, who recently died, gave him the quilt, explaining that it would protect him. Study of the quilt reveals that the designs on it are thaumaturgical symbols of protection, and while in the boy's possession, it displays a number of functions. When he hides under it, the boy cannot be perceived. When wrapped around him, the quilt protects him from physical harm. It can also slowly heal wounds. When he ties it around his neck like a cape, it allows the boy to fly. What's more, while the boy can willingly surrender the quilt, if it's forcibly taken, it returns to him in a matter of moments.

+ show block
– hide block

During his detainment, the boy also explains that the quilt protects him from "the bad things." These "bad things" are anomalous entities that manage to penetrate the site and seem to exhibit ghost-like abilities. SCP personnel discover that they're drawn to the blanket rather than the boy, as the child exhibits no anomalous qualities. The "bad things" also appear blind to the quilt when it's inert, so it's simply a matter of encouraging the child to surrender the quilt. However, SCP personnel find it difficult to convince him to give up the last thing connecting him to his family.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Aside from the fact that the quilt's anomalous properties are as limitless as the boy's imagination, the central drama of a boy getting over the loss of his family and learning to accept what happened and move on would make for a good narrative. While applying amnestics would normally solve the problem, in this case the quilt allows him to resist the amnestics, as he doesn't want to forget. Surrendering the quilt will make him safe, but it'll also be giving up a part of himself.

Additional Notes: Any assistance with formulating the anomalous "bad things" would be greatly appreciated, as that's not fully fleshed-out yet.

item.title: Phantom limb syndrome but with a twist
item.description: they can still feel...something. Something that should not be there
item.content:encoded:
Patients have never been amputated nor were they born with any missing limbs. However, they can still feel…something. Something that should not be there.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: starting out with an old version of the SCP article, along with obvious clarification that is it outdated and a new one is currently under review. Interviews that lead up to the revelation. Researchers notes / thoughts

Elevator Pitch: The premise is that this SCP is essentially a version of the Phantom limb syndrome…at least that’s what it appears to be. The difference is that it affects people who have all their limbs. Those affected people feel limbs that normally do not exist on humans, such as a third arm or leg. Some may even feel multiple ones.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: It caught the attention of some researchers, it wasn't exactly deemed a threat, since patients behaved normally, besides the weird sensations that come with feeling extra limbs.
After some more discoveries were made, the research team realized that there is a bit more to it. Not exactly dangerous, just…strange. It is more than just a sensation. Eventually, this would lead them to the realization that the SCP is not simply phantom limb syndrome but actually a sort of bridge between multiple realities. Patients are connected to lifeforms from another reality that possess the limbs they feel.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It is a very passive SCP. Not an alternate dimensions, not a crazy creature, not a disease, etc. The SCP itself is a bridge between dimensions, at least two. This opens up a lot of storytelling opportunities relating to other dimensions but more in the sense of how the dimensions interact.

Additional Notes: I'm still debating how deep I should delve into this other reality but right now, I find it more interesting if it is seen as something that the Foundation needs to explore once they find out how to actually access this reality. I’d appreciate feedback about the general idea and that kind of multiple dimension connection.

Looking forward to some feedback. Happy holidays! :)

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror/Comedy

Elevator Pitch: A mysterious software appears along with a mysterious PC out of nowhere and seems to grant mindless beings knowledge to act as sapient beings. However, they can't recall their past nor origin and seem to have only a small piece of their memories.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

This software was discovered when one of the Foundation personnel noticed strange sounds from one of the enhanced containment chambers that're containing non-sapient SCPs. They discovered that it is talking and chatting on a PC that shows up out of nowhere.

This SCP originally is a PC that appears to have an unknown chatroom with unidentified programmers. This chatroom's software is named "The Humanoids," seemingly designed for both sapient and non-sapient anomalies to interact with each other through the technology screens. Any non-sapient/mindless humanoid entities/beings who come in contact with the screen will eventually be granted the knowledge to act as beings that aren't mindless. They can also interact with others as long as the PC isn't shut down. Of course, they may also embody human nature and act like regular humans, and some act very smart.

However, despite being granted sapient knowledge, the humanoid entities cannot remember their origins, and some seem only to recall a small piece of their memories.

Attempted to delete the software or destroy the PC is proven to be impossible, for it is shown to be constructed out of mysterious unidentified materials and seemingly has a powerful firewall to prevent hackers from infiltrating into it. However, the Foundation didn't try their best efforts in an attempt to erase the software nor wreck the PC, for it is because, with the help of "The Humanoids" chatroom, the hostile non-sapient SCPs appear to have good behaviors rather than being hostile, evil, and aggressive. However, the chatroom doesn't actually change the behaviors of sapient SCPs as they still have their original personalities.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP helps the Foundation in being able to make in contact and collect some information about non-sapient hostile humanoid entities without needing to be worried about taking any risks, not large-size ones, though.

A humanoid figure looking like a starving man.

Starts off in urban Florida 2019, where the SCP was presumed to be a homeless man living on the street.
It was there for 2 years, not doing anything until it was caught trying to peel (with teeth) a local teen's skin off.
Video footage was captured (eventually uploaded online), and the SCP quickly-crawled away with the body.

+ show block
– hide block

Foundation field agents were warned and investigated after widespread local fear of SCP-XXXX online.
MTF Search-Teams found SCP-XXXX by an urban lake.
SCP's didn't eat, breathe, talk or scream, and walked on all fours similar to a spider.
It was captured by MTF. (Audio Attached)

Foundation put coverup stories, making a fake background, court charges, and sentencing.
Foundation took a list of items where SCP was recorded: Printed photos of people of ranging ages and an old coat SCP wore made of skin parts of different animals.

Research on the photos (attached) revealed the people were that of now-dead people.
People were that of children, adults, prison inmates, and one of the leading researchers of the Foundation.
Connections between lists of people could not be found by staff, but details of who they are, are given.
Hidden letters on the photos revealed words "fam", "peel", "ric", "sorrow", "controlling", "it's gone", and "give it back".
A note was found in the coat that stated "Life is given to those with lemons, a bad one is given to those with oranges".

D-class was used to experiment on the SCP, audio recordings, and experiment chart was attached.
SCP-XXXX didn't react or attack until the third experiment, where the D-Class chuckled nervously.
More experiments occurred until Foundation found out SCP-XXXX only reacts to D-class laughing at certain distances.

SCP-XXXX was watched over after every kill, in which he was seen to make shapes with the pieces of skin.
Foundation gave SCP-XXXX crayons and paper, but it only used skin to make shapes.
Recreated drawings were made (and attached), with the most identifiable ones as an orange, a house, a frowning face, and a knife.

Page Layout: Standard SCP format and addendum. The Addendum will have a journal where the main story takes place.

Elevator Pitch: My SCP shall be about a teen-aged boy (named Darcy Clover) who finds himself unable to be forgotten. All information about him has the same effect: when a person learns about it, it remains in their conscious memory forever. The memories can be ignored, but never forgotten.

The article's story will mainly revolve around Darcy's life when his anomaly manifested, shown through a digital journal he kept prior to his acquisition by the Foundation. According to his journal, Darcy was originally a normal high-school student, if a little introverted. When his anomaly manifested, however, he began to draw away from his friends and family, out of fear that they would remember him in a bad way.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The article begins with the boy's containment procedures, detailing many specific recommendations given by his lead psychologist. It then moves on to his description, noting (along with his effects) extremely antisocial tendencies and a general fear of cameras/microphones. It finally comes to a transcript of the boy's journal, where the core of the story lies.

The journal shows how he used to be a normal kid. He had mild feelings of self-doubt and issues socializing, but they never prevented him from living a normal life. That is, until his anomaly manifested. It's not known exactly when it happened, but he noticed how people began to act off around him. This "offness" became more intense over time, until people started to reference things he did that he had trouble remembering, leading him to realise that he was unable to be forgotten. He drew away from everyone he knew, drawing the attention of the Foundation as a consequence.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I personally haven't seen much relating to unforgettable anomalies, so I feel this would be somewhat new. My plan is to show how Darcy's anomaly changed his personal/social life for the worse, which I think would be interesting to read/write about.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a computer program that one day appeared and automatically installed in every computer at site-XX. If run it will display the message "SCP Breach Simulator- Site XX Edition" and then create a realistic simulation of site XX, were you will play as yourself and will have to survive a SCP breach.

Central Narrative: Any computer brought into site-XX will manifest the program inside of their files, even if the computer was completely cut out from the internet and any other method of networking. SCP-XXXX cannot be deleted but any computer that is taken outside of the site will have the program erased from its files. SCP-XXXX will work on personal computers and laptops; smartphones, tablets, servers and mainframes won't manifest the program inside of their files. On the other hand anything that classifies as a personal computer, regardless of its model, year of manufacture or Operating System will manifest and be able to run the program. Older models will create more crude simulations, with very old computers generating text based descriptions and allowing the users to chose how to act with input prompts and more modern computers generating 3D environment that can even be compatible with Virtual Reality technology.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention Grabber: The program manifested after a particularly sudden and gruesome containment breach. In that breach agent XXXX mentioned how it felt as if her actions were not her own, but chosen and forced upon her by someone else. It is believed that the simulations that the SCP generates are not simulations at all, but live feed from a parallel universe where a breach is occurring. Players from this universe take control of their versions from the universe that is being shown in the computer, and the simulation will run until the breach is contained, the SCP escapes or the "player" dies. It is believed that after running a simulation SCP-XXXX will automatically install in every computer of site-XX of that particular parallel universe, spreading itself further and further.

The foundation can choose to use the SCP to conduct breaching simulations or even spy in parallel universes and steal research or information that might help their cause, but at the cost of damaging another SCP foundation from a parallel universe and spreading the SCP more and more. The more the SCP has spread the higher the chances are for the Foundation of this universe from becoming another "simulation" and suffering a breach.

item.title: The White Glove's Limousine | Seeking Greenlights
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights : Yes

Page type : SCP Article

Genre : Drama/Mystery/Horror?

Elevator Pitch :

- An SCP that takes the form of a Mercedes-Maybach S600 Pullman Guard

- It usually appears in a handful of locations between 7 p.m. and 9 p.m, especially when the streets are crowded.

- The SCP will “target” a person out on their own, from the crowd, who will then feel obligated to seek out the car. Upon the target’s approach, a single hand wearing a white glove will emerge from the interior of the vehicle and will gesture for them to get inside.

- Once the person does so, the door will close violently. The car will then start moving again.

- It will disappear after 25 minutes of driving. A hypnotic effect distracts any human observing the car for too long after its departure. Recording the vehicle is impossible.

Narrative :

+ show block
– hide block

In 2010, the Foundation received reports of a series of mysterious disappearances around the Sydney Opera House, the Wynn and Encore complex, and the Théâtre de Paris. After long months of investigation, the dispatched agents discovered the source of the disappearances : a black limousine, presumed responsible for abducting the missing persons.

In order to determine its properties, it was deemed necessary to dispatch observation teams to all the destinations at which the anomalous limousine had been spotted. The O.T. located outside the Théâtre de Paris was the first to spot the limousine;, at 8 p.m, on the 19th of may 2010. Although the doors of the vehicle were opened upon arrival, its interior was impossible to observe due to a lack of light inside the car. A few minutes later, a Caucasian man in his 20s entered the limousine. The door then seemed to shut itself violently, and the car immediately took off. Attempts at following the object were always unsuccessful : after an average of 25 minutes of observation, any agent following the car experiences a brief moment of inattention, during which the vehicle escapes from view. Filming the vehicle also seems to be impossible : all video records in which the limousine appears seem to be heavily disturbed, and hence impossible to watch. If any person other than the target gets within arm’s reach of the vehicle, the doors will immediately clamp shut, and the car will flee the scene. To this day, this is the only known way to prevent further abductions by the object.

Attention-grabber : The mysterious limousine and disappearances.

item.content:encoded:

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP page

Elevator Pitch:

  • Our senses define and limit how we interact with reality, they do not, however, define and limit reality itself. (aka there is more around us than meet the eye)
  • Human eyes can perceive three colors of light: red, blue and green, other colors are perceived by combining these three with the intensity of the light. Other animals have different light perception and therefore can see different colors than humans. Particularly, praying mantis shrimps can perceive between 12 and 16 light colors.
  • What happens when a human receives an experimental implant that allows them to see as many colors as a praying mantis shrimp?

Central Narrative: A high level MTF agent becomes blind after a mission and becomes the perfect guinea pig for an experimental biological implant that combines human and animal DNA to create augmented agents. The article starts with a brief description of the agent and how she lost her eyesight and how the implant was created. It follows with some logs regarding the surgery and recovery of the agent.

item.title: SCP Concept: "This Last Week"
item.description: A town stuck looping the same week over and over again.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama/Emotional, possibly a little Horror (I think - hard to pin down)

Page Layout: Nothing incredibly special at this stage. If this ends up being my first published article, I don't want to be too ambitious and not be able to follow through without experience first.

Elevator Pitch: Time loop, town repeating for decades. No-one in town's aware it's happening.

Central Narrative: Loop - when first documented - lasted 1 week, resetting at midnight (internal date noted, but when undecided).

Log of events in cycle, taken not long into repeats. Includes local activities. Occasional person enters - unfortunates from before containment who didn't get out in time (e.g. Sole car enters. Driver confused because brother was in car in front, implying brother left town pre-midnight, while he didn't).

Affected bubble's temporal hazard, as anyone who enters becomes trapped in repeats if they don't leave pre-reset, arrival happening every time (shown with unfortunate agent). Living things from town cannot be removed, disappearing when extracted. Non-living objects can be, however, duplicates taking their place next repeat. Objects/people introduced from outside arrive at same time in later loops.

Speculated to be unstable spacetime bubble, causing repeats and leaking details from other realities, overwriting native. No cause determined.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Subtle changes between loops - only couple tiny things in given repeat (e.g. teapot's colour or someone's breakfast). Small things eventually snowball into drastic shifts over countless cycles - e.g. street names, businesses and even identities (extreme example's bartender originally documented as male replaced by woman). Log of noted changes over time provided, starting out with small things before they're moved to unseen comprehensive file, log's remainder focusing on significant alterations.

Article end: Researcher contacts superior. Too subtle to tell before, but they're now sure loop's shrinking. Not physical space, but timeframe, and events aren't exiting the loop - they're compressing, events getting closer together and causing problems. Example: Car driving through crossroads, another driving from other road seconds after. Compressed, crossings get closer until cross at same time, and either stop or crash. Regardless, it's a major change, causing butterflies. They speculate that as bubble grows increasingly unstable, timeframe will keep shrinking, events compacting until "casual density event" occurs. It's anybody's guess what happens then. As it isn't accelerating, however - and week's only shortened by minutes in decades - it's centuries before "event". It's suggested personnel prepare in case something emerges sooner.

'Emerges' is deliberate wording. Speculation that distortion/timeline leakage caused by something pushing into our reality.

Compression's resulted in short calm immediately pre-midnight, where there's no more events. Town disappears temporarily, leaving semi-circular crater. Was emergence of this that revealed compression.

Scp 5091 is a boy who died in 1909 but came back to life in his coffin. He suffocated from lack of air, then came back. This went on until the cemetery he was buried in was dug up and he was taken in by the foundation, who now use him as to test possible cures to different poisons/diseases.

I call him Ressurection Teddy, as a nod to the legend of Resurrection Mary. Does that count as plagiarism?

Central Narrative: The different test the foundation tests the foundation conducted on him. After being killed and coming back to life a few times, they decide to use him as a lab rat to develop cures to poisons and diseases that are currently without cures.

+ show block

The things they've tested on him are AIDS/HIV, different types of prions, ricin, amatoxin, tetrodotoxin, and even a few anomalous diseases and poisons.

The kid was already traumatized from being buried for so long, and these tests only made things worse.

During an interview, he asks where his parents are. The doctor tells him they're likely dead, and he has a panic attack and hasn't talked since. Testing was suspended, and the poor thing is being given counseling.

Where I'm at I think it would work to edit the original article adding the new instance to the description, adding a new containment procedure for the new instance, and an interview between the agent and the SCP to get some info on what seperated this guy from all the others that just get the Skywalker protocol.
